result.title: GRAZE: Text-Free Grasp Synthesis for Unseen Objects from Human Gaze
result.summary: Text-conditioned hand-object interaction (HOI) generation provides intuitive semantic control, but language is an indirect way to specify where an interaction should occur on an object. Naming the part to grasp requires object-specific words, and naming the approach side requires a reference frame that a prompt lacks. We propose GRAZE (GRAsp from gaZE), which generates hand-object grasp motion from recorded gaze instead of object and part names. Its Geometry-Aware Gaze Encoding (GeoGaze) maps gaze rays to cues on object geometry, and cross-attention conditions a diffusion Transformer on these cues. We also introduce HOT3D-Grasp, a grasp-centered benchmark with object-disjoint folds built on HOT3D recordings. On unseen objects, GRAZE grasps the target part more often than the strongest text-conditioned baseline (49.3% vs. 43.6%), achieves the highest grasp success (66.3% vs. 46.6%), and transfers without fine-tuning to GazeHOI (45.3% vs. 33.8%). Gaze conveys the approach side: when gaze is rotated around the object, the approach turns with it in 59.1% of cases, against 20.5% for a text model retrained with clock words. On the same backbone, a text prompt names parts better, but gaze adds the approach side. Given both, GRAZE keeps the prompt's part accuracy and follows gaze.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GRAZE，以记录的眼动射线经几何感知编码（GeoGaze）和 cross-attention 条件化扩散 Transformer，从视线而非文本生成未见物体上的抓取动作，并构建 HOT3D-Grasp 物体不重叠基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文把 gaze 当作指定「抓取何处、从哪侧接近」的空间证据通道，与 LVR 关注的主动感知、视觉证据定位与筛选可能有概念联系；但其面向机器人抓取运动生成，能否启发 VLM 推理期的证据条件化仍需核查。
